children: At a much-hyped event this week, Tesla
finally unveiled the new Roadster, its most futuristic automobile to date, with production expected to begin in 2028.

new Roadster is its performance flagship. Model 3 and Y were about 98% of Tesla’s Q3 deliveries. Roadster would make that lineup stronger as autonomous vehicles scale and drivers still seek a luxury driving experience behind the wheel. The potential benefit extends beyond the release itself, where the demand could improve across the company’s whole lineup.

That said, I argued in my recent article that engineering excellence and valuation require separate judgements. Over time, the brand strength needs to be supported by profitability and cash generation to support today’s valuation measures sustainably.
Julia Ostian: In my opinion, the new Roadster is not important for Tesla's
future business at all, but it is very important for Tesla's narrative, and these are two different things.

Even though, as predicted, the presentation was noticed by many people, production is only targeted for 2028, more than a decade after the first prototype was shown. And Tesla still didn't give a price for any version.
Even if it ships on time (which, looking at the history, is a big if), it will be a low-volume car with almost no impact on revenue or margins for the company. What it does do is give Tesla
a sentiment boost right before earnings, and it worked, as the stock jumped about 5% in premarket the next day.
Dhierin Bechai: The Roadster to me is more of a prestige project for Tesla

, showing off capabilities with a limited volume and niche target audience at a high price point. It is a halo product rather than something that carries substantial financial value for the company. As a result, I do not consider it to be important to Tesla's future in a financial sense.
Where it would become interesting is if it ultimately provides a justification for a combination of Tesla and SpaceX

Mike Zaccardi: I took the Roadster unveiling as more of a signaling mechanism rather than an imminent profit driver. Indeed, the technology is awe-inspiring, and the innovation pipeline is probably longer than most investors expect right now. But I don't expect to see flying cars on highways anytime soon!

title: SA Asks: How important is the new Roadster to Tesla's future?
